transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

Hi, Doctor. Thank you so much for seeing me. Um, I hope I'm not taking up too much of your time today. 

I'm here because... well, I've been having a little bit of trouble at work lately. It's probably nothing major, just me being a bit silly, but I can't seem to keep my things in order anymore. I work at a dry cleaner, you see, and... it's actually a little embarrassing to admit, but the tickets, and the receipts, the workshop notes, the customer jobs—they just sort of all get piled together on me. And then I end up just standing there, not really knowing what I'm supposed to handle first. 

Does that make sense? I hope I'm explaining that okay for you.
How much distress or anxiety do you feel when you're standing there, not knowing what to handle first at work?

Oh, um... anxiety? I don't know if I'd use a strong word like that. I really don't want to make it sound worse than it is, you know? 

It's not like I'm breaking down or crying or anything like that. I just get a little... oh, maybe flustered? Just feeling a bit silly that I can't sort it out quicker. I usually just try to smile and take a breath so my boss or the customers don't notice I'm stuck. It's really not a huge deal, I promise. 

I hope that answers your question okay? I just wouldn't call it actual distress, if that makes sense. Is it normal to get a little flustered like that sometimes?
Are you having trouble keeping things in order or feeling flustered in other parts of your life, outside of work?

Oh, um... well, maybe a little bit? I really don't want to sound like I'm complaining, I know everyone has their hands full. 

But, um, at church, I usually help lead some of the planning for our events. Recently, though, I actually sort of stepped back from doing that. I think... well, I think people were getting a little frustrated with me. I wasn't keeping the details as organized as they needed, and I really didn't want to be a bother to anyone, so I just quietly stepped down. It's fine, really, they have wonderful people handling it now, and I'm happy just to sit in the pews. 

And, um... I know I said the work thing wasn't a huge deal earlier. And I really am trying my best! But I guess I should admit that... well, the shop has had a few late orders recently because of me getting mixed up. And some of the billing got a little confused, too. It's caused a few tense moments with the rest of the staff, and maybe a couple of customers. 

I just hate feeling like I'm making things harder for everyone else, you know? I really try to keep the peace. Does that make sense? I hope I'm giving you the right kind of information.
Do you find yourself forgetting things that you would normally remember?

Oh, forgetting things? Um... no, not really. I don't think so, anyway. I mean, everyone forgets where they put their keys now and then, right? But I wouldn't say I'm losing my memory or anything like that. I try really hard to keep on top of things. 

I mean, the mixed-up orders at work, that's more just me getting... tangled up in the moment, not really forgetting the customer entirely. I hope that makes sense? I just don't want you to think I'm completely losing my mind or anything. Is it okay if I say I haven't really noticed that happening?
Do you have trouble paying attention to details in your daily activities?

Oh, um... details? Well, I try really hard to be careful, I really do. I don't want to sound like I'm just careless or not trying my best. 

But, um... well, sometimes when I'm going over the day's dry-cleaning orders... I can start out just fine, you know? But then, after a few minutes, my mind just sort of... drifts? I'll start thinking about the care labels, or maybe those choir plans I mentioned, or just something I need to do at home. And then, before I know it, I realize I haven't really been looking at the tickets in front of me, and I might have missed half of what I was supposed to check. 

It's not that I don't care about the details! I just get a little sidetracked sometimes. I always try to go back and double-check when I catch myself doing it, so it's not like I'm just ignoring it. Does that sound like what you're asking about? I hope I'm explaining it right.
Do you often feel restless or fidgety when you're sitting still?

Oh, um... restless? I wouldn't say that, no. I mean, I can sit still just fine. I really try to be polite and attentive when I'm supposed to be, like during a church service or when I'm talking to someone. 

I guess sometimes I might shift in my seat a little, or maybe tap my foot, but I think that's just normal, isn't it? Everybody gets a little stiff if they sit for too long. I definitely don't want to seem like I can't behave myself or sit quietly. I hope it's alright that I don't really have that problem? I'm trying to be as helpful as I can.
Do you often act on impulse without thinking things through?

Oh, um... acting on impulse? Like, doing things without thinking? No, I don't think I do that. I really try to be thoughtful about my decisions, I promise. 

I mean, I know some people just jump into things, but I always try to be responsible. I wouldn't want to cause any trouble for anyone or do something I'd regret. I like to think things over, especially at work or with my choir group. It's so important to be reliable, you know? 

I hope that's a good thing? I just really wouldn't want you to think I'm reckless or anything like that. Is it okay that I don't really struggle with that?
Do you often feel worried or apprehensive about things in your daily life?

Oh, worried? Um... no, not really. I mean, I think I handle things pretty well, overall. I really try to just take things one day at a time and not let myself get all worked up. 

I know some people worry about every little thing, but I always try to stay positive and trust that things will work out. I don't want to be a burden to anyone by always fretting, you know? Like at the dry cleaners or with the choir, I just try to do my part and keep a smile on my face. 

I hope that's the right way to look at it? I just wouldn't want you to think I'm an anxious person or that I can't handle my daily life. Is that the kind of answer you were looking for?
Do you often have trouble completing tasks or projects that you start?

Oh, um... completing things? Well, I always try my absolute best to finish what I start. I really pride myself on being a hard worker at the dry cleaners, I promise. 

I suppose... well, maybe sometimes if I'm given a few instructions all at once, I might get a little turned around? Like, if someone gives me three things to do—say, call the supplier, tag a silk blouse, and then enter the receipt—I'll jump right in and do the first one right away! But then, um, I usually get pulled into something else before the rest is completely finished. 

It's not that I don't want to finish them, I just want to help wherever I'm needed, you know? I hope that doesn't make me sound irresponsible or like a bad employee? I really do try to be as helpful as possible and get back to it eventually. Does that make sense, what I'm saying? I hope I'm answering this right for you.
Do you find it hard to focus on one thing for a long time?

Oh, um... focusing for a long time? Well, I always try really hard to pay attention, I promise. I want to make sure I'm doing a good job, especially at work. 

I guess... well, sometimes if I'm looking over the day's dry-cleaning orders, I start out just fine! I'm really focused on getting it right. But then, after a few minutes, I might just... kind of drift a little bit? Like, my mind might wander to the care labels, or maybe what we're singing in choir this week, or just things I need to do at home. And then I'll look back and realize I might have missed half of what I was supposed to check. 

But I always go back and fix it! I really don't mean to lose focus, I just get so interested in all the little details around me. I hope that doesn't sound like I'm not taking my job seriously? I really do care about doing good work. Is it okay that my mind wanders a bit like that?
Do you often have difficulty sustaining attention on tasks or activities in your free time, outside of work?

Oh, um... in my free time? Well, I really try to stay busy and productive, you know? I like to think I have a lot of interests!

But, um... I guess it's a little bit like what I was just saying about work? Like, if I sit down to read a book or maybe do a little puzzle at home, I start out with the best of intentions. I really do! But then, after just a little while, I might find myself thinking about, well, the choir plans again, or maybe remembering a stain I couldn't get out at work, or just... anything else, really. And before I know it, I haven't turned a page in ten minutes. 

It's not that I don't like my hobbies! I just... I get so easily sidetracked by all the other things going on in my head. I hope that doesn't make me sound lazy or like I can't enjoy things? I really do try to stick with them, I just have a hard time staying put sometimes. Is that... is that normal for someone my age? I hope I'm giving you the right kind of examples.
Do you think your difficulty with organization and staying on task is more related to having trouble paying attention or to something else entirely?

Oh, um... gosh, I'm honestly not really sure? I guess I haven't ever stopped to think about exactly *why* it happens. 

I always just told myself I was being a little, well, scatterbrained, maybe? Or maybe just trying to juggle too much at once because I want to be as helpful as I can. I don't really know if it's because of the attention part or... or something else entirely. I've never really been able to figure it out myself. 

I really hope it doesn't just mean I'm, well, bad at my job or disorganized on purpose, you know? I try so, so hard to keep everything straight at the dry cleaners, I promise I do. I just... I don't really know the reason behind it. What do you think it sounds like? Am I making any sense at all?
Do you think your mind wandering and getting sidetracked is the main reason you have trouble with organization and tasks?

Oh, um... well, maybe? I suppose the mind wandering might be part of it... but honestly, the main thing, the reason I actually made the appointment, is just that I... I can't seem to keep my work area in order anymore. 

I try really hard to be neat, I really do! But somehow, it just gets away from me. I'll have the dry-cleaning tickets, and then the register receipts, and my little notes from the workshop, and the customer jobs... and suddenly they're all just sort of piled together on the counter. And then I stand there and I just... I don't know what to handle first. 

It looks terrible, and I know it does, but I promise I'm not a messy person by nature! I just get a little overwhelmed when it all stacks up like that. Do you think that's because my mind wanders, or is it just me being a little clumsy with my paperwork? I hope it doesn't sound like I'm making excuses for a messy counter...
Do you think your trouble with organization and tasks is mainly because you have trouble paying attention to details?

Oh, um... paying attention to details? I... I'm not really sure if that's the main reason. I mean, I don't think I miss the important details, mostly? 

I really do try to be careful, especially with people's nice clothes. I always double-check the care tags and make sure I know what the customer asked for. I don't want you to think I'm careless with the garments, because I really do take pride in doing a good job! 

But... maybe it's just that when there are so many little details all at once, like the tickets and the receipts and the different piles... I just sort of lose track of how to organize them? It's not that I don't see the details, I just... I don't know how to keep them all tidy. Does that make sense? I hope I'm answering your question right. I just wouldn't want to say I'm bad at details when I try so hard to be thorough...
Do you think your difficulty with staying on task is mainly because you have trouble focusing your attention?

Oh, um... focusing? I guess maybe that could be part of it... I mean, I really do try to stay focused, I promise! I don't want to sound like I'm just daydreaming on the job. 

But... well, sometimes I'll start going over the day's dry-cleaning orders, and I'm doing just fine at first. But then, after a few minutes, my mind just sort of... drifts? I'll start thinking about the care labels, or maybe what we're singing in choir this week, or just something I need to do at home. And then suddenly I realize I haven't really been looking at the tickets in front of me, and I might have missed half of what I was supposed to check. 

I always catch it and go back, though! I make sure everything is right in the end. It's just that my mind likes to take little walks, I suppose. Do you think that means I have trouble focusing, or is it just normal for your mind to wander a bit when you're doing routine things? I hope it doesn't sound like I'm not taking my work seriously...
Do you have trouble staying organized and on task at home, in the same way you do at work?

Oh, um... at home? Well, I try my very best to keep things nice everywhere I go, really I do! I wouldn't want you to think I'm just leaving messes all over the place... 

But, I suppose... well, it does spill over a little bit, maybe? At the shop, it's gotten a little tricky lately. A few orders have been late, and the billing got a tiny bit mixed up... just a few times! And there have been some, oh, I guess you'd call them tense moments with the staff and a couple of customers. I felt just awful about it, I really did. I hate letting people down. 

And, um... at church, too. I've always loved helping with the planning committees, but I actually stepped back from leading some of the events recently. Some of the other ladies were getting a little frustrated with me because I was having a hard time keeping all the sign-up sheets and schedules straight. I just thought it would be better for everyone if I let someone else take the reins for a while. 

I hope that doesn't make me sound terribly irresponsible... I just want to make sure everyone is happy and things run smoothly. Do you think it's okay that I stepped back from the church planning, or should I have tried harder to push through it?
Do you think your difficulty with organization and tasks is more because you have trouble sitting still and being patient, or because you have trouble keeping your mind on what you're doing?

Oh, um... sitting still? I... I don't know if I'd say I have trouble being patient, exactly. I really do try to be respectful when people are talking, I promise! 

But... well, maybe it's a little bit of both? It's just... I do find it awfully hard to just stay in my chair for a long time. Like, when we have our church committee meetings, or even those fabric-care training seminars for work... everybody else just sits there so nicely, taking notes. And I try, I really do! 

But then I'll just think, "Oh, I should get a quick glass of water," or "I need to go grab that other stack of papers," or "I should just go check on that one thing real quick." I always have a good reason for getting up! It's never just to be disruptive. I just feel like I need to be doing something, you know? Moving around a little bit. 

I always make sure I don't interrupt anyone when I do it, though. Do you think that's terrible of me? I just... I get this sort of restless feeling in my legs, and getting up seems to help me focus better when I sit back down. Is that okay, or should I really be forcing myself to stay put the whole time?
Do you think your mind wandering and difficulty with tasks is more because you have trouble paying attention or because you're easily overwhelmed by the tasks themselves?

Oh, um... overwhelmed? Oh my, I hope I don't come across as someone who can't handle a good day's work! I really do try my hardest to take everything in stride, I promise. I'd hate for you to think I'm just throwing my hands up the second things get a little busy at the shop. 

To be perfectly honest, I'm... I'm not really sure which one it is. I haven't really thought about it quite like that. The tasks themselves aren't too difficult, really, especially since I've been doing them for a while. So I don't know if I'd say I get *overwhelmed*, exactly... I mean, I always try to keep a smile on and just get through it! 

So maybe... maybe it is just the paying attention part? I just sort of... lose my place, even when I'm trying my absolute best to stay right on track. But I really couldn't say for sure which one is the main culprit. 

I hope that's an okay answer? I want to be as helpful as I can, but I'm just not entirely certain. Do you think it's alright that I don't quite know why it happens? I hope it doesn't seem like I'm just making excuses for myself...
Do you think your main problem is that you have trouble paying attention or that you act on impulse without thinking?

Oh, goodness... acting on impulse? I... I really hope I don't do things without thinking! That sounds so reckless, and I always try my very best to be considerate of everyone around me, I truly do. I wouldn't want you to think I'm just, oh, doing wild things or making snap decisions at the dry cleaners with people's nice clothes. I try to be so careful! 

So, um... I honestly couldn't tell you which one is the main problem. I just don't know. I haven't really noticed if one is worse than the other, to be perfectly honest, or if I even do the impulsive thing very much at all. 

I'm so sorry, I feel like I'm not giving you very helpful answers today. Is it alright if I'm just not sure about this one? I hope I'm not making your job too difficult by not knowing exactly how to explain it...
Do you think your main difficulty is with paying attention to what you're doing or with interrupting others and acting on impulse?

Oh, interrupting? Well... I suppose I might do that just a little bit. But I really, truly don't mean to be rude! I always try to be so polite with everyone at the shop. 

It's just... sometimes when the younger staff are talking, or if I see them sorting the delicates, I just sort of... step in? Like, I might reach over and fix a pile of silk blouses before they even ask for my help, or I might chime in on their conversation because I have an idea that might help them. 

I know it probably comes off like I'm butting in, and I feel just awful about it afterward. I really do! I just want things to be done right so our customers are happy, you know? I get so eager to help that I just kind of jump in before I think. 

Do you think they think I'm being terribly bossy? I really hope not. I just want to be helpful... is it very bad that I do that?
